families.topic: screening of patients and contacts for Candidozyma auris
evidence_points: The guidance sets out patient and contact screening recommendations for C. auris.
It addresses risk-based screening, sampling sites, repeated screening and management of discharged contacts.
The page links screening to readmission flags and infection-control communication.
The guidance forms part of the national 2025 update.
The source is an official GOV.UK primary page managed by UKHSA.
The page was live-opened successfully on 31 July 2026.
Screening intensity should reflect exposure, setting and local transmission evidence.
A single negative screen does not automatically exclude colonisation in every circumstance.
A positive screen does not by itself establish invasive disease.
Final decisions require exposure history, sampling quality, timing, repeated results, clinical status, IPC controls and documented review.

Treatment choices require current susceptibility evidence and specialist clinical judgement.
Patient movement and transfer controls should not delay urgent necessary care.
A historical positive result alone does not determine current clinical severity.
